experiments.title: 1. OCR engine bake-off and the hybrid choice
experiments.purpose: Pick the OCR engine for the two drawings. Priorities: digit fidelity, line boxes, no invented text, Traditional Chinese with CAD variants, tiny coloured pipe labels, local runtime.
experiments.method: Ground truth: 115 strings (81 sys sheet, 34 raft sheet), 40 marked CRITICAL, read by eye from 3-4x zoomed crops. Sheet-wide fuzzy match: hit = at least 85 % of GT characters recovered; digit % = share of numbers in the GT string found intact. Position-restricted zone test on the raft pipe-label band (7 CRITICAL strings). Same page handling for every engine. PP-OCR: 1280 px tiles, 160 px overlap. VLMs: 640 px tiles, 120 px overlap, 2x zoom. Variants: unclip ratio 2.0 and 2.5, 2x upscaled tiles.
experiments.dataset: ocr115 (115 GT strings, 40 CRITICAL; ground truth lives in docsearch/modelsel/gt.py, drawing text only)
configuration: PP-OCRv6 medium with unclip 2.0 (the hybrid base).
Hybrid: HunyuanOCR re-reads only tiles holding at least two lines below 0.75 PP-OCR confidence (docsearch/cascade.py).
Hybrid default selected by DOCSEARCH_OCR_ENGINE; single-engine fallback ppocrv6-m-u20.
experiments.environment: M1 (RTX 3060 12 GB, shared, with a few CPU cores). Timings from concurrent jobs on one GPU.
experiments.duration: Per-engine seconds for both sheets are in the table. Hybrid: raft sheet 858 s, sys sheet 187 s (hybrid.log, measured). PaddleOCR-VL sys sheet alone 2,209 s.

rows: Solid baseline, weaker than v6 on digits.
Rejected: upscaling hurt hits and was 3x slower.
Best single engine: best digits, fastest. Fallback.
More hits, fewer intact digits; not chosen.
Rejected: missed text on dense CAD, 0/7 on the pipe-label band, very slow.
Poor on tables and formulas; best on tiny coloured pipe labels (5/7); slow, loops, Simplified script.
Hybrid: PP-OCRv6-m-u20 + HunyuanOCR on unsure tiles
Current default. Raft pipe-label band 1/7 to 4/7. CRITICAL digits fell (96.7 to 95.3 overall). Costs 858 s on the raft sheet and +4.3 GB weights.

experiments.judgement: OCR is not the main answer bottleneck. In a check of 16 wrong answers (hand-graded run), the correct value was already in the OCR text for 11. The hybrid is the best measured balance on these two drawings, not a claim of universal superiority. The digit regression is unexplained.
caveats: 115 GT strings from one annotator, two sheets from one project; single runs do not establish reliable ordering.
Matching is sheet-wide, so repeated labels are credited from any occurrence; only the zone test is position-restricted.
VLM numbers are for one prompt and one tiling each.
Timings were measured with concurrent jobs on one GPU; indicative only.
The same drawings and questions were used while tuning prompts and indexing after failures.

experiments.title: 4. Chunk reading-order fix (index v2) and the determinism repeat
experiments.purpose: Fix a real chunking bug (block grouping linked a line two lines away across an overlapping neighbour, so a value could sit under the wrong heading) and check whether the index change moves accuracy.
experiments.method: Same 40 questions, same LLM, same seed (0). v1 chunking: 662 chunks. v2: 1,246 chunks. Repeat with the same seed to measure determinism.
configuration: Index v2, top-12, seed 0, facts off.
Repeat run: same configuration.
experiments.duration: Mean 187 s (v2-order) and 183 s (v2-order-run2 by file mean 182.5 s), from the results files.

rows: net effect of v2 on accuracy
zero within noise; 3 questions flipped each way (Q020 among them)

experiments.judgement: Kept because the bug was real. Accuracy did not move. The repeat is not a clean determinism test: the two result files disagree on grader counts (13 vs 20 pass) and on 7 grades.
caveats: MODELS.md section 0 says the repeat was byte-identical. The staged result files do not support that for grades; the difference may come from re-grading after grader fixes (commit f052a04, 2026-11-16). Not verified.

findings: More chunks did not help: top-30 gave about 21 correct against 22 for top-12 on the same 38 (4B).
A larger reader alone did not clear the bar: 9B at top-12 gave +3 over 4B on 38, below the +4 net needed to count as better.
Fact rows gave +5 for 4B on the development set (22 to 27 of 38, none lost) and +2 for 9B (25 to 27). The fresh paired test decides whether they go on by default.
OCR is not the main bottleneck: in 16 wrong answers the correct value was already in the OCR text for 11.
Sampling noise is about 1 to 2 questions net (seed 1 vs seed 0).
Still wrong with fact rows: near-identical tanks (Q040, Q041, Q043, Q044, Q045); pump C bore (OCR reads 5 for 3); connecting-pipe count (Q143); false NOT FOUND (Q113, Q115); Q037.
Failure classes: near-identical tanks, wrong totals, counting, false NOT FOUND, OCR misread of the pump bore.
